full_judgment:
4. Pursuant to the service of the Rule, the learned Advocate Mr Idrisur Rahman entered appearance on behalf of the respondent No. 5 namely S Hedayetullah, the Managing Director of Taj Jute Backing Company Ltd and the respondent No. 6, AKM Nazmul Hossain (Mostaque) and preferred affidavit-in-opposition jointly wherein it has been stated, inter alia, that Annexure-A is not an agreement, rather a memorandum of understanding (MOU) which the respondent No. 5 executed with the writ petitioner for transferring the shares of him and the other private share holder of Taj Jute Backing Company Limited and upon such memorandum of understanding (MOU) the respondent No. 5 procured a "No-objection' from the Ministry of Jute, Annexure-C to writ petition in his favour to transfer the said shares under certain terms and conditions and thereafter came to an agreement with the petitioner on 20-5-1999, Annexure-B, under which the writ petitioner was made liable to comply those terms and conditions. But since the writ petitioner failed to comply with those terms and conditions of the Annexure-B, as he admitted in Annexure-12, appended to the affidavit-in-opposition, the respondent No. 5 could not comply with the terms and conditions of Annexure-C and, as such, the Ministry of Jute lawfully rescinded the said 'No-objection'. It has been further stated that in the meantime the loan giving Uttara Bank obtained a money decree against the management of Taj Jute Backing Company Ltd for default in repaying the loan money and through executing the said decree since the Bank failed to sell the entire concern of Taj Jute Backing Company Limited to any prospective buyer, now the said Bank has made private negotiation with respondent No. 6 for private sale of the said shares of Taj Jute Backing Company Ltd and meanwhile, during the pendency of this writ petition, the negotiation in respect of the sale of the shares of Taj Jute Backing Company, held by the respondent No. 5 and his co-holders of shares has been materialised subject to result of this writ petition. It has been further categorically denied that the writ petitioner complied with any of the terms of Annexure-B as evidenced from the admission made in Annexure-12, a letter written by the writ petitioner, and also stated that Uttara Bank has cancelled their 'No-objection' through Annexure-15 accorded earlier to the respondent No. 5. 

 6. The respondent No. 3, Uttara Bank, has also entered appearance through the learned Advocate Mr SM Abdur Razzak who preferred affidavit-in-opposition. The case of the respondent No. 3 that the Taj Jute Backing Co Ltd is a defaulting borrower of the said Bank against whom Uttara Bank Ltd instituted mortgage Title Suit No. 30 of 2001 and obtained decree on contest on 7-7-2002 and through executing the said decree in Arhajari Case No. 73 of 2003 they have made advertisement for public auction for entire concern of Taj Jute Braking Co Ltd But, failing' to get any purchaser of the same, they have negotiated with respondent No. 6 for sale of the private shares of Taj Jute Backing Co Ltd to him. It has been categorically stated that earlier Uttara Bank has issued a 'No-objection' to the respondent No. 5 to transfer the private shares of the said company to the writ petitioner upon certain terms and conditions, but since the respondent No. 5 failed to comply with those terms and conditions the said 'No-objection' was later cancelled. In the meantime the possession of the entire concern Taj Jute Backing Co Ltd has been handed over to the respondent No. 3 Uttara Bank though the Court, pursuant to the provision of Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 and, as such, this Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 14. The learned Advocate Mr SM Abdur Razzak while opposing the Rule on behalf of the respondent No. 3 Uttara Bank, submits that the Uttara Bank has allowed considerable amount of money as loan to Taj Jute Backing Co Ltd and since the said business concern defaulted in paying back the said loan, the Uttara Bank obtained a decree from the Artha Rin Adalat against the said company, but upon execution of the said decree the Bank failed to procure any purchaser to sell the said concern in public auction and thereafter, privately negotiated with the respondent No. 6 to sell the assets and liabilities of the Taj Jute Backing Co. Ltd including its privately owned 58.52% shares which has been finalised. But due to the Rule of this writ petition it could not be materialised and, as such, the Bank is facing irreparable loss and injury.
